embeddings.title: ChatITP
embeddings.text:
ChatITP
At Chat ITP, we aim to utilize the potential of generative artificial intelligence to celebrate and continue the rich creative tradition of the NYU Tisch International Telecommunications Program (ITP) that spans over two decades. We are building an open-source large language model (LLM) trained on a comprehensive archive of creative media artwork — including video, sculpture, writing, animation, game design, and virtual reality. Our goal is to reflect the collective creative spirit of the ITP community.

We are committed to ethical innovation. We ensure that all creative works are included in the training set only with the explicit permission of their creators, thereby respecting the integrity and ownership of each contribution. We see Chat ITP as a dynamic crossroads of past, present, and future creativity, providing a glimpse into the entire history of ITP’s exploratory journey.

Chat ITP serves as a public research project, a living historical archive, and a continuous creative resource for students, faculty, and alumni. Beyond our immediate community, Chat ITP stands as a proof-of-concept for other institutions, showing the potential of generative AI to interact with and enrich creative archives. We aim to inspire wider appreciation and application of artificial intelligence in celebrating and advancing human creativity, from university programs to museums.

In the end, Chat ITP will function as a generative AI creative engine, situated on a multimedia archive of student work. It will provide new ways to engage with art, inspire innovative creations, and deepen understanding of the evolving relationship between technology and human expression. This project aims to empower current and future generations of creators, educators, and innovators, making creative exploration accessible to everyone.

Cara Cai

embeddings.title: Only sings in the dark
embeddings.text:
Only sings in the dark
A musical instrument made of a wall of LEDs that you play holding solar panels.
Octavio Figueroa Moya

embeddings.title: Hover Craft
embeddings.text:
Hover Craft
How can the process of creating music be as frictionless as possible? Can an interactive musical experience be constructed in a way that activates a user’s reward pathways to create a positive association with the act of making music? Can an experience be developed that is so fun and easy that it inspires non-musicians to try and learn an instrument? 

"Hover Craft" seeks to answer these questions. As part of the artist's thesis project, this first version of the experience focuses on the physical fabrication and basic functionality of the piece. Users hover their hands over a screen to create a music and light show as if by magic. Users can also control parameters such as the current instrument, scale, chords, and arpeggios played for a highly replayable experience meant to foster a love of the art of making music.
Andre Lira

embeddings.title: The Red Line
embeddings.text:
The Red Line
The Red Line is a device that illustrates the shifting thresholds for taking drastic action in response to current events. Inspired by the idea of a "red line"—the concept of a boundary that shouldn't be crossed, it gathers news articles in real-time from various news sources, analyzes and produces scores for them, and displays the current "state of affairs" in Israel (my home country) on a live meter. Users can set a movable "red line" on the meter, visually marking the point where they'd need to take action—such as leaving the country or engaging in civil disobedience—in response to worsening conditions.
Jasmine Nackash

embeddings.title: Persephone's Cuisine
embeddings.text:
Persephone's Cuisine
Persephone's Cuisine, a sub-project of the thesis Spring; Worm; Worm, features a 3D-printed pomegranate dish as a canvas for projection mapping. Inspired by the myth of Persephone, the dish comes to life with projections of cells trying to connect to each other, inviting viewers to interact with its symbolic, ever-shifting surface while savoring the dish.
Jiayi Li

embeddings.title: Three Minutes
embeddings.text:
Three Minutes
“A watched pot never boils” is a proverb often said in a moment of anxiously waiting for something to happen, and it feels as though it never will. In response to that, we say, “Yes it does!” 

Presented in an arcade-style cabinet, our take on the proverb reverses the activity of boiling water from passive to active, requiring the user to sit in front of the encased kettle that only boils when both buttons are actively pressed. When the water has boiled, the user can slide open a drawer that contains Japanese green tea, a tea cup, and saucer. 

This project is part of Absurd Hotel, an assignment brief for NYU ITP’s Fall 2024 Designing the Absurd course taught by Pedro Galvao Cesar de Oliveira

angela juarez

embeddings.title: The Unreal Engine Audio Experience
embeddings.text:
The Unreal Engine Audio Experience
"The Unreal Engine Audio Experience" is a gamified audio-visual program which allows users to affect sounds using a video game controller. This experience is meant to invite playful experimentation, and will create a community-driven work of art.
Noa Kirschbaum

embeddings.title: Snow Motion
embeddings.text:
Snow Motion
Our winter show will feature a dynamic collection of works created throughout the semester, showcasing a diverse range of animation techniques including flip book animation, stop motion, collage animation, and more.
Anna Chen

embeddings.title: Momentum
embeddings.text:
Momentum
The project presents an innovative, body gesture-based audio-visual performance that responds in real-time to the audience’s movements as they dance with the music. Using a combination of machine learning techniques—including body pose detection, body segmentation, text generation, and image generation—the work aims to create a surreal, chaotic, yet playful experience that invites active participation.

TouchDesigner serves as the primary platform to integrate and execute these models, generating dynamic visuals that transform based on audience interaction, resulting in an responsive visual that feedbacks repeatedly from the audience.
Luna Chen

embeddings.title: Emotion Protocol
embeddings.text:
Emotion Protocol
“Emotion Protocol” explores the tension between humanity’s rich emotions and societal pressures, particularly in Eastern cultures, to suppress and eliminate individual emotions. Inspired by the Chinese saying "喜怒哀乐" (joy, anger, sadness, happiness) and Buddhist four-faced Buddha statues, the piece fuses traditional symbolism with programmed mechanisms.

The rotating Buddha heads symbolize the paradox of emotional vulnerability within a mechanized, structured existence. Emotions, while often overwhelming and unpredictable, are integral to the human experience. This work invites viewers to embrace their authenticity, find strength in vulnerability, and remember that we are human after all.
Ziggy Yang

embeddings.title: mecha mecha mecha
embeddings.text:
mecha mecha mecha
mecha mecha mecha is a modular livestreamed performance lecture whose components pull together a playful, rigorous engagement with cuteness and clothing as scholarship. mecha mecha mecha departs from theorist Alex Quicho’s use of the mecha as a metaphor for “climb[ing] into and pilot[ing] this already-existing subject that has the unique privilege of being greater than us all, yet thoroughly downplayed and underestimated.” The talk will be punctuated with quotes for the vibes.

Vinh Nguyen

embeddings.title: Where You Linger
embeddings.text:
Where You Linger
"Where You Linger" is an interactive diorama that explores our relationships with time when we are engaged with our work. Inside the diorama, which the user sees through a peephole, is a Pepper's Ghost projection of a person engaging in different activities at a desk. 

The user is able to alter the passing of time within the diorama, which reflects how fleeting time can be when we are focused on a task at hand. This creates a different experience for each user depending on where they choose to linger in the model.
Bethany Wu

embeddings.title: Bloom Cup
embeddings.text:
Bloom Cup
Bloom Cup is a mechanical cup that is also a sound reactive kinetic sculpture. The cup's petals fling up and block anyone around the cup when they are speaking, preventing contamination.
Astro Lee

embeddings.title: Big Bad Wolf
embeddings.text:
Big Bad Wolf
An interactive interpretation of the childhood tale of the Three Little Pigs, readers are encouraged to flip through and play with the physical components to explore the story from the wolf's point of view.
Helen Lin

embeddings.title: DJ Music Box
embeddings.text:
DJ Music Box
A music looper that plays back music stems from 3 different tracks. Players are able to mix 7 different stems (2 melodies, 2 beats, 3 vocals) to "remix" songs and simulate a DJ experience.

Justin Johnson

embeddings.title: Continuum
embeddings.text:
Continuum
This project is an interactive installation combining physical screen mechanics with digital physics simulation. A screen mounted on spring-loaded mechanisms allows users to tilt and manipulate its orientation. A Unity-rendered scene displays marbles that respond precisely to the screen's physical angle, rolling and colliding with realistic momentum.

Accelerometer and gyroscopic sensors translate the screen's movements into computational responses, creating a seamless interaction between physical input and digital representation. The system uses advanced physics simulation to generate marble trajectories that match the exact gravitational forces implied by the screen's tilt.

The installation creates a direct, intuitive interface where physical gestures immediately influence a digital environment. Marbles cascade, tumble, and collide in real-time, responding to the most subtle changes in screen orientation with fluid, mathematically precise motion.
Michael Culleton

embeddings.title: Trails Overhead
embeddings.text:
Trails Overhead
This work explores the concept of presence and perception beyond physical architectures. A piezoresistive sensor mat on the floor above detects and stores the trails of people's movements on it. These trails are translated in real time into silhouettes displayed on the floor below, creating a vertical opening through the ceiling connecting two parallel spaces.
Audrey Oh

embeddings.title: Collective Composite
embeddings.text:
Collective Composite 
Step onto a pressure switch and become part of a collective portrait. This interactive installation captures your portrait, randomly selects one cell from a 7x7 grid, and prints that fragment on thermal paper. Place your printed piece onto the corresponding position on our LED-lit display grid, adding to a growing, layered community artwork.
Unlike carefully curated selfies, this project introduces chance and collective contribution. Using face detection and custom image processing, your full-color portrait is transformed into a high-contrast thermal print that harmonizes with others on the display. As portraits accumulate and overlap, individual identities blend into a dynamic representation of our community.
The simple act of stepping, receiving your printed fragment, and adding it to the grid connects you physically to this evolving artwork. Through this process, your individual portrait becomes part of something larger – a temporal expression of collective identity that changes throughout the show.

Fabrizio Guccione

embeddings.title: Let Your Mind Draw
embeddings.text:
Let Your Mind Draw
See how your mind flow visually and physically. Using EEG headset to detect the brainwave and communicate with Arduino and stepper motors to draw on physical canvas.
Luna Chen

embeddings.title: Enchanted Fractal Forest
embeddings.text:
Enchanted Fractal Forest
Enchanted Fractal Forest is an immersive 360-degree interactive installation combining generative audio and video. It connects the dots between the fractal geometry of nature and music, encourages experimental play, and invokes the enchanted mystery of a forest at dusk.
Jesse Fischer

embeddings.title: The Great Circular Revolution
embeddings.text:
The Great Circular Revolution
"What if the world becomes circular?" Set in the year 2200, The Great Circular Revolution is a fully hand-drawn animation that explores humanity's drastic and surreal attempt to achieve peace by eliminating all things square. This satirical and humorous short film questions human nature, the oversimplification of complex problems, and the pursuit of utopian ideals through absurd means. 
The story unfolds in a dystopian yet oddly whimsical future where squares are declared the ultimate source of misery
This animation critiques humanity's tendency to seek simple solutions for profound existential issues, emphasizing that societal harmony cannot be achieved by merely changing forms. The circular world may appear utopian, but its absurdity highlights the complexity of peace and coexistence. 
Through striking visuals and playful narration, The Great Circular Revolution serves as both an entertaining spectacle and a thought-provoking reflection on human desires, ideologies, and the lengths we might go to achieve an elusive sense of harmony.

Laurel Fang

embeddings.title: MIND CONTROL
embeddings.text:
MIND CONTROL
Mind Control is an immersive audio-visual experience that allows participants to conceptualize and interact with their own brain activity…and to experiment with and test their ability to assert control over it. Colorful LED lamps are synchronized with digital animations and tones in order to represent states of mind such as focus, meditation, and clarity. These states are each triggered by the participant's EEG readings – allowing the user to control the experience with their mind. The complete experience consists of three phases; an initial calibration period consisting of calming breathing exercises and a general introduction, a self-observation period during which the only interaction is that between their brain activity and the various audio/visual states, and a final phase during which they can use a physical controller to navigate between states freely – exploring what each variation has to offer and potentially using them to affect their actual mental state. The process aims to provide the user with space for both passive observation of their own cognitive activity, as well as the opportunity to experiment with actively controlling it. 
Gelala Adali

embeddings.title: Mirror & Me
embeddings.text:
Mirror & Me
A reflected image of a mirror raises people's awareness of the surrounding space and their connection to others. A concave mirror encourages self-reflection by focusing attention inward, while a convex mirror reveals more of the environment and the people within it. Using the nature of reflections, we let users rediscover and rebuild their connection to the shared space and the community around them.
DJ Kim

embeddings.title: Temple of Fortune
embeddings.text:
Temple of Fortune
The Temple of Fortune is an interactive installation that invites participants to explore the intersection of tradition, symbolism, and storytelling. Inspired by Chinese cultural practices, the project delves into the art of fortune-telling and the rituals surrounding offerings at temples. By engaging with symbolic choices and immersive elements, participants are encouraged to reflect on the values and narratives embedded in these traditions.

At its heart, the project celebrates the meaning behind rituals and their power to connect individuals to history, culture, and spirituality. The interactive design transforms ancient practices into an engaging, contemporary experience, offering a bridge between past and present. Participants are guided through moments of introspection, where they consider how their choices resonate with personal and collective values.

Through symbolism, storytelling, and interaction, The Temple of Fortune aims to foster a deeper appreciation for cultural heritage while sparking curiosity about how these traditions continue to shape identity and community.
Queenie Hsiao

embeddings.title: 100 Days of Making Class Show
embeddings.text:
100 Days of Making Class Show
100 days. 100 projects. 16 students.

Students were offered the opportunity to pursue a creative passion and develop or refine a skill over a 100-day period. Selecting their own prompts, they created and uploaded something new every single day for 100 days.
Isabella Celleri - Bonilla

embeddings.title: Mute Sentiment
embeddings.text:
Mute Sentiment
I took inspiration from Esther Perel, a writer on the subjects of intimacy, fantasy, and imagination. On the topic of communication, she says that speech is currently the favored medium, and that the modern focus on verbal communication is perhaps flawed. Male and female education around emotional expression is skewed, and resulting social constructs restrict men’s verbal expression and trap women in a constant state of verbal expression, the “prison of words.”

Through this work, I wonder if non verbal communication or bodily communication can hold up as an alternative to verbal expression. In my piece, the external, closed off form expresses frustration with constant talk, while the organic, flowing internal form— accessible only through touch— represents the soul or state of being. 

Xara Alexander

embeddings.text:
Hot Air

Hot Air is an interface proposal: ideas and phrases collected during the process of ideation are blurred and then made clear only when approached with care and patience, accessed via an unclear and amorphous medium - air and latex.

embeddings.title: Erosion
embeddings.text:
Erosion
Erosion draws inspiration from places destined to vanish in the future due to rising sea levels.
The sound piece incorporates samples from the Dead Sea, blending them with complementary sounds to create an evocative auditory experience.
The performer interacts with sea creatures, crafting an improvised yet composed sound performance.

Audrey Chou

embeddings.title: As Above So Below
embeddings.text:
As Above So Below
As Above So Below is a Multisensory VR journey that invites participants into the liminal experience of a seasoned astronaut on the brink of returning to Earth.
Participants sit on a rocking chair and travel through a space elevator, where they must make a pivotal decision: ascend or descend. Their choice determines their destination—either a serene, cozy environment offering comfort and calm or a strange, intense space filled with the bizarre. Each room symbolizes a distinct path back to "normal" life on Earth.
In this room, they’re asked to wait patiently for a cookie to bake in a small oven—a test of their ability to embrace everyday rhythms after the vast, timeless void of space, and to understand their relationship with delayed gratification. Their success in waiting rewards them with a warm, grounding taste of home - the cookie.
Baiyuan Xing

embeddings.title: The Sinetactophone
embeddings.text:
The Sinetactophone
The Sinetactophone is a collaborative audiovisual instrument inspired by the Theremin and experiments with the Terpistone. Two users utilize the movements of their body to generate and manipulate the instrument’s output through ultrasonic waves. The instrument combines the user interface of a theremin with the techniques of a synthesizer, allowing for looping tones and adjusting parameters, creating an evolving audiovisual environment shaped by their interaction. Paired with a projector, it immerses the players in a mix of sound and visuals, exploring how people respond to consistent audiovisual feedback. The design and interaction of the instrument aims to blur the line between human and machine, enhancing the ability of the two musicians to express emotion with their bodies in collaboration. Two users stand on opposite sides of the instrument, using the it to collaborate on the sound and visuals that the instrument produces.
Alyssa Kalbus

embeddings.title: The Last Rice Plant Harvested By Human Hands
embeddings.text:
The Last Rice Plant Harvested By Human Hands
The year is 2029. In the mountainous region of southern Anhui Province lies Huizhou, a place renowned for its centuries-old agricultural traditions. Known for rice cultivation, tea production, and sustainable forestry, Huizhou’s unique landscape and climate have given rise to farming techniques rooted in harmony with nature, soil preservation, and resource efficiency.

The Chinese government has recently introduced precision (AI) agriculture and widespread robotic farming, automating rice cultivation across the nation. This transformation displaced humanity’s role in the Sancai (三才) — the Taoist relationship between heaven, earth, and humankind — a guiding principle for traditional Chinese agriculture for generations.

This shift reflects China's broader narrative: a nation that has, over the past three decades, used technology to lift millions out of poverty and create a more equitable society. Automation in agriculture is heralded as a blueprint for other developing countries, showcasing technology as a tool for systemic change. This is what Sinofuturism seeks to unpack: “What do we lose when machines take our place in traditions that once defined our connection to the land?”
Senaida Ng

embeddings.title: Tis the Brain
embeddings.text:
Tis the Brain
This is a analog automaton designed to visualize the chaotic and intricate workings of the human brain. Through the interplay of acrylic materials and a meticulously crafted gear mechanism, this project illustrates the complexity and unpredictability of human thought. The mechanical aesthetic reflects the intertwined relationship between humanity and machinery, showcasing how analog systems can beautifully mimic the organized chaos of the mind. Entirely battery-free, CogniChaos highlights the raw, tactile essence of mechanical motion as a metaphor for cognitive processes.

Proud Aiemruksa

embeddings.title: خنثى (Third Gender)
embeddings.text:
خنثى (Third Gender)
7ft x 4ft large canvas with 50 photographs of male and female models cross-dressing pinned on as well at 2 poems inscribed on metal sheets stuck on. The project is an exploration of the concept of non-binary through a Saudi-specific lens. It takes on topics of religion, women's rights, gender-norms, and queerness from my perspective as a first-gen Saudi-American. Project is in-process of being finalized, will be finalized by Tuesday 12/10/2024.
Maan Algarzae

embeddings.title: Baby Mac
embeddings.text:
Baby Mac
A MacBook and a baby MacBook exist. The participants must take care of the baby MacBook while the mother MacBook rests. However, the MacBook does not want the baby MacBook to leave its line of sight even while resting. The main goal for participants is to care for the baby MacBook without letting it cry, while meeting the mother MacBook's demands.
Wonjung Choi

embeddings.title: What Tomorrow Do We Have Left
embeddings.text:
What Tomorrow Do We Have Left
"What Tomorrow Do We Have Left" is an art installation that blends physical sculpture and digital media. The piece is an hourglass form constructed from birch plywood, coated in white plaster. A crack in the upper cone invites the viewer to peer inside, revealing a digital screen that displays a video of the artist gazing directly at them. This intimate encounter establishes a profound connection, where the act of viewing becomes a mutual exchange. The artist considers this work a self-portrait in the form of sculpture and video, encapsulating his identity and personal experience within the piece.
Mingze Gao

Fragments of Us
Fragment of Us is an installation that explores shared dreams and memory. Visitors are invited to make their way into a physical space that represents collective memories and feelings of nostalgia. The space responds to and reflects the unconscious influence we have on one another, exploring the fragile, often unseen threads that bind us together.

embeddings.title: Elon Simulator
embeddings.text:
Elon Simulator 
Elon Simulator offers a glimpse into a future where high-quality media production costs approach zero, and the speed from idea to execution becomes instantaneous. What new media formats will emerge in this reality?

In Elon Simulator, you step into the shoes of the richest and most polarizing man on Earth. You’ll make decisions on Elon’s behalf and witness where they lead. Will you buy twitter? Become a better lover? Seek a more peaceful life? Or will you continue on your path, perhaps even attempt to “save humanity”—but at the cost of your own?

embeddings.title: Good Enough
embeddings.text:
Good Enough
This artwork symbolizes internal pressure. It reflects the idea that achieving our goals requires a certain amount of inner pressure to drive us forward. However, too much or too little pressure can become an obstacle to success. The balloon represents our goals, while the air filling it symbolizes the internal pressure needed to realize those aspirations.

More than a painting
More than a painting.

embeddings.title: The Wishing Pond
embeddings.text:
The Wishing Pond
The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams. - Eleanor Roosevelt 

The Wishing Pond is an enchanting artistic installation designed to rekindle the magic of wish. Embark on an age-old East Asian tradition of wish-making with water lanterns, reimagined through a harmonious blend of history and innovation. Through the gentle glow of LEDs, the touch of force-sensitive resistors, and a fun harmony of sound effects, The Wishing Pond invites participants to make a heartfelt wish for their health, success, love, family and friends, or wealth. The sincerity of your wish will ignite a dazzling water lantern show based on Chinese culture, a shimmering response to your purest hopes. Wish with all your heart, and let the light guide your dreams to life!

Tina Yu

embeddings.title: Grandma's Round Belly
embeddings.text:
Grandma's Round Belly
Grandma's Round Belly is an immersive VR installation inviting the audience to watch a five-minute VR short film while physically embracing a tactile, round object representing my grandma's belly. Through this project, I explore themes of family, love, and my connection to long-distance home. The story begins with a dream I had on the New York subway, where I found myself returning to my grandparents’ old house. Blurring the boundaries between dream and reality, the narrative unfolds through five scenes and three cherished memories inspired from my grandma's round belly and the traditional Chinese home. As the VR film progresses, the audience gradually senses the warmth of my grandmother and traces of her life. The story concludes with a simultaneous embrace of my grandmother’s belly in both virtual and physical world. I hope this project evokes a sense of warmth in the audience, awakening hidden love and treasured memories within their hearts.
Yuntian Zhao

embeddings.title: かたちたち (Shapes)
embeddings.text:
かたちたち (Shapes)
A series of softonic sculptures that play the sound of human breath by feeling each other's weight on the theme of human relationships in everyday life. During the last spring semester, tensions and arguments arose among students over the department's handling of wars currently happening. During this process, while I witnessed conflicts and broken friendships due to differences in ideology, I also witnessed situations where people eventually came to understand each other and reconciled through physical contact. This experience deepened my interest in how people with different ideologies build and repair relationships. In my thesis project, I hope to visually and sensually express the process of understanding that transcends language and the subtleties of emotion that arise in this process.
Sao Ohtake

embeddings.title: CanvasCollective
embeddings.text:
CanvasCollective
CanvasCollective is an interactive, community-based web platform that's all about sparking consistent creativity among artists at every skill level. Our mission is to get people drawing regularly through weekly prompts that challenge and inspire. It's a place where you can post your artwork, see different interpretations of the same theme, and connect with fellow creators. We compile everyone's contributions into animated collages that really highlight our community's collective vision. We are excited to host a space where creativity flourishes and everyone can see the impact of working together.
Andy Cabindol

embeddings.title: Veinsight
embeddings.text:
Veinsight
Veinsight consists of a ring and cuff that transform the wearer's heartbeat into a visual rhythm of pulsing LED lights. The wearable piece explores the metaphor of "wearing one's heart on their sleeve," reimagining it through technology to create a tangible manifestation of our internal states.
The wearable piece investigates the body's role as an honest messenger of our emotional world. While we often struggle to articulate our feelings verbally, our physiological responses—particularly our heartbeat—reveal what we might not yet understand or be ready to express. In moments of connection, attraction, or vulnerability, our pulse quickens before our conscious mind processes these feelings.
By making the heartbeat visible, this piece creates an intimate dialogue between the wearer's internal state and the external world. The synchronized LED lights serve as a bridge between the private and public self, encouraging a reflection on emotional vulnerability and the ways we choose to reveal or conceal our true feelings in relationships.
Kyung Jin Han

embeddings.title: Interactive StoryTelling in the Ghanaian context
embeddings.text:
Interactive StoryTelling in the Ghanaian context
Interactive Storytelling based on the Ghanaian context. My focus is to delve deeper into the oral traditions that have shaped Ghanaian  Arts and culture for millions of years. My particular focus is on Anansi stories, which are widely known among the Ashanti people of Ghana and extend to the general Ghanaian folklore.
Caakyire Kyei Baffour

embeddings.title: MODERN INTIMACY: FIND YOUR MATCH
embeddings.text:
MODERN INTIMACY: FIND YOUR MATCH
MODERN INTIMACY: FIND YOUR MATCH

What does intimacy look like in a world dominated by dating apps, social media, and generational divides? This playful mobile quiz invites participants to swipe through questions about love, sex, connection, and consent—exploring how our experiences of intimacy are shaped by culture, technology, and time.

Designed with the swiping gestures of a dating app and the tongue-in-cheek charm of a BuzzFeed quiz, this project creates a space for reflection and curiosity. Participants answer intimate questions, confronting assumptions and reconsidering what intimacy means in their own lives. The only demographic data collected is generational affiliation, allowing participants to see how their perspectives align—or diverge—from those of other generations.

The experience is anonymous, encouraging honesty and vulnerability. At the end of the quiz, users are shown their “matches”—a playful insight into the ways intimacy shifts and resonates across generational lines. 

Data will be used to inform the author’s research for an ongoing art installation proposal about the modern landscape of intimacy. 
Angelique Axelrode

embeddings.title: OBJ
embeddings.text:
OBJ
The light-and-shadow art piece explores the dehumanizing topic of objectivization. The interplay of light and shadow captures a haunting duality, reflecting a profound sense of nothingness and an aching desire to dissolve into obscurity.

Using a paper cutout as a foundation, layered projections symbolize the internal emotions of the person in the image, as well as the thoughts of others about them. Over time, the light outline of the person fades, disappearing entirely after being overrun by these external perceptions. This transformation reflects the devastating effect of unwanted attention: the more one is perceived in ways they do not wish to be, the stronger the desire becomes to escape perception altogether.

“My face is an object so visible it’s embarrassing.” 
- A Breath of Life, Clarice Lispector
Diana Kereselidze

embeddings.title: UrMind
embeddings.text:
UrMind
The game is a brainwave-interactive experience where players control a small creature and use their brainwaves to manipulate various 3D environments while navigating through challenges and exploring different rooms. The goal is to provide players with an immersive experience of brain control, helping them understand how to meditate, calm their minds, and focus.

By amplifying certain sensory elements that people often overlook during everyday thinking or meditation, the game encourages players to become more aware of these distinct mental states. At the end of the journey, players will gradually learn how to better manage and optimize their own mental states.
Taigen Jin

embeddings.title: I Got Your Back
embeddings.text:
I Got Your Back
In this day and age where we are inundated by ubiquitous and instantaneous communication, we invite you to an experience where you communicate with others word by word, one letter at a time. As the user gauges how keenly they can decipher a tactile message, it symbolizes how even the smallest units of communication can be misunderstood and highlights the amount of focus needed to comprehend someone else’s intentions.
If you have faith and ‘lean into’ the experience, there’s a higher chance you will fare better at getting the message right. We got your back!
Jiyou Park

embeddings.title: Reel It In
embeddings.text:
Reel It In
Can you trust your friends? Will you cooperate, or betray the group? Will a shared common resource always be used up when everyone has access?  

This playful fishing game invites you to grapple with questions of trust, resource management, and the fragile interplay between individual actions and collective consequences. It’s a hands-on lesson in game theory and social psychology, disguised as a fun challenge.

The primary inspiration is the Tragedy of the Commons - the idea that if many people are responsible for maintaining a finite public resource, they will naturally use as much of it as possible and ultimately destroy its value altogether. This theory is often used in the context of environmental problems, such as overfishing and deforestation.  

In this game, you and your friends take on the roles of fishermen sharing a single pool of fish. Each round, the fish will reproduce—up to a limit—offering an opportunity to earn points by pressing your button to catch one. But beware: the more you take, the fewer fish remain to replenish the pool. If the pool is emptied, everyone loses.

There are opportunities to gain points for cooperation too, but it will require patience and self control. Are you ready to put yourself to the test? 
Julia Ming Yuet Kan

embeddings.title: The Harbinger of Joy
embeddings.text:
The Harbinger of Joy
Harby, short for the Harbinger of Joy, is a robot puppet. She is controllable through The Orb of Movement. She follows the Orb's exact movements to destroy towers of blocks, except for her tendency to twirl and penchant for whimsy. Can YOU top the destruction score chart as fast as possible… Or will you succumb to her infectious silliness?

Noah Dorazio

embeddings.title: TinyDesk VJ
embeddings.text:
TinyDesk VJ
TinyDesk VJ brings live performance to life through a tactile interface. Powered by p5.js and ML5 body segmentation, it integrates live video with surreal digital effects that you can dynamically control. The interface features rotary encoders, faders, potentiometers, and buttons, allowing you to layer effects like rain, ripples, lasers, and lightning in real-time. Whether you’re performing alongside music or exploring interactive art, this tool offers endless possibilities for creativity. Experiment with the controls, combine elements in unique ways, and watch as your inputs transform into exciting, ever-changing visuals.
Olivia Lee

embeddings.title: Behind Family Planning Policies: A Data Visualization Project
embeddings.text:
Behind Family Planning Policies: A Data Visualization Project
The data visualization website provides different angles to understanding global family planning programs with interactive data charts and a narrative storytelling. By comparing datasets and literature works, it focuses on discussing the necessity and long-term influences of China's then one-child policy, including comparing with countries with a similar birth rate but milder family policies and the truth behind its negative influences on sex ratio at birth. It invites the audience to look at a long-lasting historical event in a fresh, critical, and visual way and tributes to the people who experienced it or grew up within it.
Chanel Feng

embeddings.title: Alter for Loved Ones
embeddings.text:
Alter for Loved Ones
Inspired by the common cross-religious practice of gracing one's food before eating, Alter for Loved Ones is a place to pause and honor our technology and the infrastructure surrounding it, before we consume it, and before it consumes us. 

The pace of technology and the magnetic nature of our screens often does not allow for us to pause and consider what makes up the technology we use daily. Visit the Altar to pay respects, reflect, grieve, and ultimately acknowledge the infrastructure of our technology we see all around us, where it comes from, who it's made from, and how it can be used. 

A meditation on what, how, if, we can, alter…

Meghna Mahadevan

embeddings.title: Autotune for Drummers
embeddings.text:
Autotune for Drummers
"Autotune for Drummers" is an exploration of music and time, using specialized, custom made electronic drumsticks. This experiment offers a solution for drummers who play live with a computer, a very common practice these days that is extremely challenging and demands almost superhuman ability from the drummer that has to keep perfect sync with the computer.
These drumsticks use sensors and microcontrollers to guess the drum hit before they actually occur and send a MIDI note in the next 16th note, keeping the drummer always on time. This results in snapping or “quantizing” the drum hits to the beat whether the drummer is pushing (hitting too early) or dragging (hitting too late), virtually going back in time and correcting the drummer even before they actually hit the drum.
Andy andtheNIGHT

embeddings.title: Trace
embeddings.text:
Trace
Size Updated!
After a rain, the ground briefly holds the marks of water splashes. They slowly fade away under the sun and wind, leaving only a transient impression. This disappearing act makes me think about how short-lived and fragile traces can be in our lives. A lot of the things we do or experience are just like raindrops hitting the ground—creating a momentary ripple, but soon fading away as if they were never there. These impermanent traces remind me of the marks we leave in life: some vanish into memory, others linger in corners we can't see.

Through this piece, I want to invite people to reflect on the transient and fleeting nature of things. Even though many of our actions may not be remembered forever, they still leave behind unique marks, even if just for a moment.
Max Sun

embeddings.title: Anxiety balloons
embeddings.text:
Anxiety balloons
The Anxiety Balloons is an interactive installation designed to explore and reflect on the emotional states of participants through a combination of typing game, inflating balloons, and visualizing anxiety levels as weather patterns. Inspiration from personal experiences of moving from calmness to anxiety while working on code assignments. It encourages users to reflect on their inner state and observe how external actions like typing can mirror emotional shifts.

- How It Works
1. Typing Section
Participants type their thoughts, and a final anxiety score (0-100) is calculated based on three factors:
·Color Selection: Choose a color representing your current state. Warm tones suggest higher anxiety, while cooler tones reflect calmness.
·Sentiment Analysis: Powered by the ml5 Sentiment Model, the text is analyzed to assign an emotional value.
·Pressure Sensor: Records typing force, where higher pressure indicates greater anxiety.
2. Scoring Representation
The final score combines the three elements, with sentiment analysis carrying the most weight. The score is translated into a weather type that symbolizes the participant's emotional state:
1-25: Clear Skies 
26-50: Partly Cloudy 
51-75: Stormy Skies 
76-100: Thunderstorm 
3.Balloon Inflation 
Use programmable air inflated balloon in real time. The longer the typing duration, the larger the balloon grows
4. Stickers
At the end, users can take a sticker that matches their weather-based emotional score or attach it to their balloon as a personal reflection of their anxiety balloon.

- Purpose
This project transforms a routine activity like typing into a reflective experience, encouraging participants to become more aware of their emotions, recognize patterns of stress, and find a sense of balance within themselves. It serves as a gentle reminder to acknowledge feelings and cultivate emotional self-awareness in the midst of daily routines.
Siyan Chen

embeddings.title: Rūpa
embeddings.text:
Rūpa
Rūpa is an exploration of the tension between collective and personal memory, as well as the subjective nature of emotional truth. On stage, alone, I stand before a mirror, seeing what appears to be a complete image of myself. Yet, as I turn away, the mirror shatters, each fragment reflecting a distinct version of how I was seen through the eyes of others: a child, a student, etc. Each one embodies a unique emotional projection, a subjective "truth" born of their relationship with me.

Shifting between perspectives—mine and theirs—becomes a way to navigate the friction of these memories, exposing the gap between who I think I am and the interwine of how I exist in others’ minds.

Through these cracks, I glimpse the fragile tension between breaking and becoming. Rūpa is not just my form—it is the echo of my self, fractured by others’ views, yet yearning for wholeness.
Jiachen Zhou

embeddings.title: Bowing Lamp
embeddings.text:
Bowing Lamp
Bowing Lamp is an interactive piece that responds to your movements. When you bow to the lamp, it tilts forward as if bowing back to you and turns on its light. It’s a playful way to show how even simple objects can feel alive and connected to us. Inspired by Kenya Hara (原 研哉) and Kenji Kawakami (川上 賢司), this bowing lamp is designed for the first "Absurd Hotel" to be opened in Japan. Bowing Lamp incorporates the traditional Japanese gesture of bowing, a symbol of respect and courtesy, into its design. As a site-specific installation for the "Absurd Hotel", it connects cultural values with interactive design, inviting guests to experience a playful yet meaningful exchange rooted in Japanese hospitality and etiquette.
Cassidy Chen

embeddings.title: Rolling Mail Service
embeddings.text:
Rolling Mail Service
In today's hyperconnected world, technology has brought us closer than ever, yet many of us feel more isolated. While we are surrounded by endless streams of information, true moments of human connection are rare.
The Rolling Mail Service is a mobile mailbox for the regeneration of community and connectedness. It invites participants to engage in an analog exchange of heartfelt messages, fostering unexpected moments of warmth. Each letter carried thoughts and feelings by anonymous strangers remind us of our shared humanity.
They participate, even become part of an invisible support and networking system, just by reading and answering letters from these pen friends. That simple act converts isolation to cohesion through the Rolling Mail Service, leaving us with something tangible to know we will never be alone.
Bairui Su

embeddings.title: Chromadance
embeddings.text:
Chromadance
Chromadance is an audiovisual experience where individuals are encouraged to connect more deeply with their senses through movement. By facilitating synchronization between what is seen, heard, and felt, the installation visual’s abstract kinetic expression invites inner self into the outer world.
Naodan Hu

embeddings.title: Vignette
embeddings.text:
Vignette
Have you ever wished to preserve your memories in vibrant orbs, as portrayed in Inside Out? Vignette is an interactive installation that transforms this idea into reality. Drawing inspiration from the psychology of memory, our project explores the implicit and explicit systems that define human recollection. Implicit memories capture unconscious habits and emotions, while explicit memories store conscious experiences. Through emotional connection and reflection, Vignette bridges these systems to make memories tangible.
The installation invites users to input a cherished memory into a textbox and select a color that resonates with it. This color generates a unique visualization in the form of a pom-pom, symbolizing the memory. Participants then place their memory within a display box, where it is preserved as part of a collective, immersive experience. Using p5.js, projection mapping, and Arduino, Vignette brings storytelling to life, blending technology with personal reflection.
Jennifer Huang

embeddings.title: Dreams Gallery
embeddings.text:
Dreams Gallery
Dreams are among the most intricate and chaotic realms of human imagination. 

This project is an AI-driven art gallery where you can freely explore the space, interact with the gallery's chatbot curator, and even create dreamscapes of your own. 
The aim is to delve into the parallels and contrasts between human and AI cognition, offering a unique interpretation of your dreams. Whether you're peeking into someone else's dream or seeing your own suspended like a collectible masterpiece on the wall, the experience invites reflection: do you feel like a subject being analyzed by AI?

Beyond its artistic ambitions, this project also ventures into the possibilities of AI in game development and AI-driven art installations, paving the way for new intersections of technology and creativity.
Xinyu Zhang

embeddings.title: Third Place
embeddings.text:
Third Place
For the last few years, I've found myself making miniature cities. Some appear in games, others in textiles, always with a few features in common: an apartment building, a workplace, somewhere communal. A street, a sidewalk, lights and birds and lines of laundry. An abstracted, encapsulated version of the life I've built here in New York over the past decade, and the habits that make up my days. 

I wanted to draw on that idea of smallness, intimacy, and tactility in this piece, a joint final project for my Physical Computing and Fabricating Mechanical Automatons classes. One discipline engages with the question of how electricity can animate and activate, while the other is proudly analog. Here, I attempted to blend those seemingly contradictory approaches, along with techniques borrowed from arcade cabinet and diorama fabrication, to simulate the gestures of a life — its inarticulable joys and sorrows and routines. 

I want to do more with this little world, and am genuinely honored if you spend some time with it. (Also: I hope it's fun to press the buttons!)




Alanna Okun

embeddings.title: Breaking Point - Human Population
embeddings.text:
Breaking Point - Human Population
"Breaking Point: Human Population" is an interactive installation that visualises the tension between Earth's human carrying capacity and the relentless growth of human population. Drawing inspiration from projected data and narratives about global population dynamics, the project explores this concept using a physical input where the user directly squeezes a model of the earth leading to a possible breaking point. By allowing users to physically interact and feel the relationship between pressure and fragility, the project invites reflection on humanity’s impact on the planet.
Sai Ram Ved Vijapurapu

embeddings.title: Thread
embeddings.text:
Thread
Thread is an interactive artwork that explores the lifecycle of creation, told through a single line drawing. On the screen, a line begins as a sapling, grows into a tree, and is eventually harvested and transformed into a guitar. Participants control the story by pulling a physical rope, causing the line to move and the drawing to progress. When the rope is released, the line rewinds, and the image reappears, mirroring the cyclical nature of growth and renewal. The journey concludes with the guitar playing music, blending nature’s story with human creativity.
Han Bao

embeddings.title: Surfing My Memory Web
embeddings.text:
Surfing My Memory Web
Surfing My Memory Web is an interactive musical archive of my memories of the internet. Movement of the body is detected by a web camera and used to navigate visually through different technology aesthetic sketches I've collaged together using personal media I've recorded across devices, applications, and social media sites. 
Sharell Bryant

embeddings.title: Hortensias
embeddings.text:
Hortensias
Hortensias is an interactive story about loss and life. A mobile narrative game that centers around the  real conversations of three women—a grandmother, a mother, and a daughter—reflecting on their memories of a loved one who has passed away.

Tatiana Jiménez

embeddings.title: Tri-Color Drawing Robot
embeddings.text:
Tri-Color Drawing Robot
Tri-Color Drawing Robot is a three-wheeled omni-directional drawing robot. Visitors can scan a QR code to connect to the robot and take control over some aspects of the robot. The final drawing will be a collaboration between the robot and the visitors who interacted with it.
Jack B. Du

embeddings.title: Rising River VR Experience
embeddings.text:
Rising River VR Experience
Rising River is an AI-driven self-analysis VR experience, which integrates Jungian shadow theory and the VIA Character Strengths framework to create a novel approach to therapeutic self-analysis. It began with a question: Can gaming and virtual reality democratize the therapeutic benefits of Jungian shadow work, making them accessible to a broader audience?

Jung's shadow theory highlights the neglected, subconscious aspects of the self, often tied to fears, motivations, desires, and memories. To bring this concept into an interactive experience, we designed a gaming-based self-reflection process to help players confront their shadow. The VIA 24 Character Strengths framework provided a detailed taxonomy of traits for players to evaluate as strengths or weaknesses. 

We leveraged generative AI to enrich this personalized narrative journey in VR, guiding participants through self-exploration. By answering a mix of fixed and dynamic questions, they work to revive a dried-up, dark river. Their responses, reflecting their inner selves, take shape as tangible elements in the virtual world through immersive physical interactions.


Andrew Trousdale

embeddings.title: As we fade
embeddings.text:
As we fade
“As We Fade” is an immersive audiovisual experience inspired by the science of planetary nebulae and the cosmic cycles of creation and transformation. Drawing on interdisciplinary work in cosmology, the project explores the transformative beauty of a dying star, drawing parallels to the human experience of life, memory, and death. While death is often perceived as daunting, this experience seeks to uncover its inherent beauty and inevitability. The narrative flows through ethereal clouds that give rise to stars, which collapse into scattered particles symbolizing fragmented memories. These particles gather to reveal a bedroom—a fleeting glimpse of human intimacy. Viewers are invited to interact with the particles, leaving their own imprint within the cycle. The loop returning to the clouds invites reflection on the cyclical nature of life and its enduring legacy. Rooted in scientific principles and blending the cosmic with the personal, the experience underscores the interconnectedness of existence, revealing that the profound beauty found in stars also resides in humanity.

Annelise Lee

embeddings.title: Echos of Infinity
embeddings.text:
Echos of Infinity
Traditional storytelling often unfolds in a linear fashion, with fixed narratives predetermined by creators. Echoes of Infinity, however, represents a paradigm shift, using AI to empower stories that are dynamic and deeply interactive. Players become co-creators, shaping a living, breathing world influenced by their choices. The result is a medium that blurs the lines between creator and audience, opening the door to individualized content that mirrors the complexity of human experience. Our project showcases AI's transformative potential in creating and consuming content and our ever-shifting relationship with technology. It invites players to explore a mysterious, ever-changing world while redefining their role in storytelling itself. This is more than a game; it’s a step toward a future where media is as unique and multifaceted as the individuals who consume it. 

Note: *Although the world and the societal dynamics are entirely customizable, we have borrowed characters from the show “Arcane” for the sole sake of training consistent and stable LoRAs for our image generations.*

James & Jindi
Jindi Chai

embeddings.title: Unbound from Gravity
embeddings.text:
Unbound from Gravity
"Unbound from Gravity" is a multisensory VR experience that immerses players in the thrilling world of mech combat. Step into the cockpit of a powerful mech, where intuitive controls and a fully interactive environment allow you to feel every moment of action. The experience is enhanced with haptic feedback, making every movement and impact come to life, whether you're maneuvering your mech or engaging in intense battle. This experience allows players to escape the gravity of everyday life and immerse themselves in a world where they control a powerful machine, blending fantasy with the reality of everyday challenges. Break free from the weight of everyday responsibilities and experience the rush of a high-stakes battle in a world where anything is possible.
Weichen Shen

embeddings.title: Light Garden
embeddings.text:
Light Garden
With three keywords of ‘Customizability’, ‘Collectibility’, and ‘Modularity’, Light Garden is an interactive LED product with which users create their own unique lighting experience by selecting and arranging their favorite nature-themed light objects in the garden’s base. Each piece becomes part of a growing collection, allowing users to continuously evolve their light garden’s arrangements.
Jakyoung Goo

embeddings.title: Basket Stats
embeddings.text:
Basket Stats
Basket Stats is an interactive basketball project aimed to help players keep personal stats. “How can I make stats fun and accessible for players and ultimately enhance their motivation to play basketball?” This project is designed for amateur basketball players who love to play and wish to get better at it.
Jin Yi

embeddings.title: Motherland Mother Land
embeddings.text:
Motherland Mother Land
This project is an installation that reflects on China's evolving family planning policies and their impact on women's autonomy. Over the years, these policies have undergone significant changes: from the enforcement of the one-child policy (1978–2015), to the allowance of two children (2016–2021), and now to campaigns encouraging women to have a third child. The commonality found in the change is that family planning policies have always been deeply intertwined with the state's developmental objectives. Although the state advocates for gender equality, the real gender equality can hardly be achieved because behind the family planning policy is the indoctrination of stereotypical gender roles — i.e. women as mothers.

Drawing inspiration from the history and realities of reproduction in China, this installation features a uterus placed on a set of stairs. The uterus inflates and deflates rhythmically, with the pace of the pump changing as viewers approach, symbolizing the external pressures exerted on women’s reproductive agency. The stairs are scattered with propaganda materials from the one-child policy era, alongside objects such as intrauterine devices (IUDs), representing the coercive measures used to enforce the policy. In the background, contrasting visuals from campaigns promoting the three-child policy highlight the drastic shift in the state's reproductive messaging.

This installation underscores how women’s bodies, their reproductive rights, have been subjected to constant state scrutiny, leaving them with limited autonomy over their reproductive choices.

Next to the project is a webpage showing my research results on reproductive rights.
Yelena Ye

embeddings.title: before I know it I am already
Kiss Orchestra
embeddings.text:
Kiss Orchestra
Kiss Orchestra is an installation that aims to explore the synesthetic relationship between our sense of hearing and touch in a playful manner through an instrument that features curious textures and is played using a lesser-used body part. The result is the “kiss board”, a A synthesizer pad that you can play by kissing. There two boards in the installation, one with comfortable textures which is paired with strange and unpleasant sounds, and another with uncomfortable textures but is paired with pleasant and beautiful sounds. 
Beatrice Mai

embeddings.title: Normal Paper Towel Dispenser & Normal Trash Bin
embeddings.text:
Normal Paper Towel Dispenser & Normal Trash Bin
Normal Paper Towel Dispenser transforms an everyday object into an unpredictable, seemingly sentient character. Gutted and modified from the inside, this dispenser hyperbolizes common frustrations with "automated" technologies. Sometimes it dispenses too much paper, overwhelming users; other times, it offers just a tiny shred, leaving them frustrated. Occasionally, it gets "shy," pulling the paper back just as someone reaches for it. Is it sentient? Is it being provocative? Or is it protesting the excesses of our consumption?

By disrupting the mundane act of grabbing a paper towel, the project invites playful interaction and reflection on our relationship with technology and consumption. It humorously challenges expectations, sparking laughter, curiosity, and even mild irritation. Through its erratic behavior, the dispenser anthropomorphizes automation, transforming routine functionality



Normal Trash Bin is a trash bin that gets indigestion and spits what you throw back out.

Mark Chan

embeddings.title: Interactive Generative Art
embeddings.text:
Interactive Generative Art
Made by p5.js and ML5, this project creates generative art using different algorithms, such as fungi mold, oscillating rotation, and the flocking algorithm. These generative arts can be interacted with by capturing hand motions to change their pattern and the movements of particles for extra entertainment.
Hyunwoo Nam

embeddings.title: BLOOD CHILD
embeddings.text:
BLOOD CHILD
BLOOD CHILD is a web-based interactive visual essay about a "monster" created from menstrual blood. Through an infinite-loop journey, you will traverse the creature’s birth and unbirth, experiencing the interconnections of life and death, the self and the other.

Inspired by Mary Shelley's iconic 1818 novel Frankenstein, and taking on a feminist reading of the story as maternal horror, BLOOD CHILD explores a somatic relationship with birth and death through the lens of menstruation. 

While everyone is always one step closer to death, menstrual blood —– the monthly shedding of the uterine lining, its tissues, and blood –– serves as a unique metaphor for the cycle of decay and renewal. It becomes an embodiment of both birth and death, intertwined with tenderness and pain.

Mengna Da

embeddings.title: To You
embeddings.text:
To You
To You is an audio/visual experience built in Unity about what
people would like to say to a person who is no longer present in their lives. I hope this experience can be relatable and give a meaningful touch to people upon a part of them that is fragile but memorable. Moreover, to celebrate the bravery and the
communal experience of sharing.
Julia Xu

embeddings.title: Signs
embeddings.text:
Signs
Illuminated AI-generated crop circle designs laser etched on fleece in readymade planter stands.
Nathan Townes-Anderson

embeddings.title: 2fan 1985
embeddings.text:
2fan 1985
Have you ever felt that someone next to you on the subway is peeking at your phone screen while you're scrolling through social media? In response to this familiar discomfort, I created the “2fan 1985” Phone Add-On.

Crafted from wood and aluminum, the 2fan 1985 draws inspiration from the Privacy Screen Protector, which allows visibility only to those directly in front of a device. My design offers an analog twist on this concept. The device features a phone holder with two wooden fans, one on each side. At the press of a button, the fans simultaneously open to block the view from both sides, giving users a sense of privacy in shared spaces.

This project was developed as part of NYU ITP’s Fall 2024 Designing the Absurd course, taught by Pedro Galvao Cesar de Oliveira.


Andres Franco

embeddings.title: Untouchables
embeddings.text:
Untouchables
Reach out and touch the untouchables, right wing strongmen that have risen to power across the world and are eroding national and international courts, making them unaccountable for the crimes they commit against their own people and other countries, to benefit themselves and their billionaire supporters. 
Dean Issacharoff

embeddings.title: Reality Glitch
embeddings.text:
Reality Glitch 
This interactive audio-visual installation allows audiences to use a game controller to control both sound and visuals. The installation draws inspiration from the phenomenon of AI hallucination and media manipulation, creating a space where viewers become active participants in the degradation of reality. This is a visualization of the distorted information we received today.
Jiawen Wang

embeddings.title: Seeing Time: Exploring Time-Space Synesthesia
embeddings.text:
Seeing Time: Exploring Time-Space Synesthesia
What does time look like to you? This interactive website invites users to uncover if they experience time-space synesthesia—a phenomenon where time takes on spatial form in the mind’s eye. For those who do, the project provides a platform to visualize and share their unique perspectives of time.

Through user submissions, the site displays a growing gallery of visualized time, highlighting the vast diversity—or surprising commonalities—between individuals’ mental maps of sequences like days, months, or years. The project also challenges the dominance of the Gregorian calendar by introducing alternative cultural views of time, encouraging users to question why we adhere to certain systems. Is it because they’re intuitive, efficient, or merely traditional?

As the first phase of a larger research initiative, Seeing Time seeks to collect and analyze these visualizations, asking whether patterns emerge or if each person’s relationship with time is entirely unique.
By blending technology, art, and human insight, this project turns an abstract concept into something tangible, sparking curiosity about how we perceive and shape time in our minds—and what that says about us as individuals and as a society.

Reverie Nedde

embeddings.title: LEZU
embeddings.text:
LEZU
This project is an instrument that transforms the 39 letters of the Armenian alphabet into melodies, blending cultural heritage with sound design. It features two parts: one inspired by the Armenian duduk, a traditional wind instrument, and the other by a modern MIDI controller.
Each letter is assigned a natural sound, like whistling or wind, which can be played by blowing into the duduk-inspired section. The MIDI-inspired component allows further interaction, bridging tradition with modern technology.
The instrument reflects the significance of the Armenian language, created in 405 CE by Mesrop Mashtots, an Armenian linguist and monk, to preserve a nation's identity. By turning the alphabet into music, this project reimagines the language through a new lens, offering a way to keep its memory alive while sharing its unique beauty with the world.

Lusine Kirakosyan

embeddings.title: Chromacaster
embeddings.text:
Chromacaster
The Chromacaster combines wearables with performance in a live-reactive audio visual piece of equipment worn on the arm and upper shoulder. Motion is the sixth sense, an interaction I hope to bring away from the screen and onto the body. Using the same electronics as an effects pedal, amplitude is read from a 1/4 inch jack input and converted into an LED VU meter on the forearm. And like a pedal, an output jack routes to an amp or PA system. The entire system is battery powered and lightweight, capable of casual wear on the street.   I'm tired of indie white t-shirt performances. Let's expand the equipment slot.   
Jonathan Gu

embeddings.title: Mia's Day
embeddings.text:
Mia's Day
Mia’s Day is an interactive video game inspired by individual struggles in finding the delicate balance between personal needs and those of others. It invites players into Mia’s life, a college student navigating through the complexities of relationships, self-care, and emotional vulnerability. Each player's decision will direct to a unique storyline and may trigger chain reactions; some choices may seem trivial, but every action carries weight. 
The project explores and showcases AI tools in multiple creative areas, including scene and shot design, character design, image generation, animation generation, etc. Mia’s Day creates an immersive experience that users explore and navigate through their own narration. It inspires introspection about their own lives. 
Jingyi Chen

embeddings.title: күрээн (kyreen)
embeddings.text:
күрээн (kyreen)
Kyreen is a VR experience inspired by my Sakha heritage and recent reflections on life, death, and cultural identity. In Sakha (Yakut), kyreen means “funeral,” and this piece envisions a celebration of death that blends tradition, personal history, and modernity.

The project is rooted in my experience visiting Blagoveshchensk, where I rediscovered the beauty of the city’s symbolic blue churches and malls—a hue tied to Eastern European identity. It also reflects my journey of embracing my Yakut roots, a culture I once felt hesitant to acknowledge due to its “exotic” and remote associations.

Kyreen imagines a techno-infused funeral—a symbolic event that celebrates the end of life as joyously as any milestone, merging the aesthetics of Blagoveshchensk and the stark beauty of Siberia. With vibrant visuals, soundscapes, and cultural motifs, it turns a solemn ritual into a celebration of identity and continuity, completing the circle of life.

This work challenges the traditional fear and sadness associated with death, reframing it as an opportunity to honor origins, celebrate individuality, and embrace cultural pride. 
Jingbo Ma

embeddings.title: The Tomb of Wayward Images
embeddings.text:
The Tomb of Wayward Images
When code malfunctions, it is treated with little respect, either thoughtlessly replaced with its successor or tossed away entirely. Aside from temporary anger, no thought is given to this small loss of ‘life’. ’The Tomb of Wayward Images’ seeks to question these moments of loss, taking the form of a website ‘graveyard’ that honors image files that have broken and been lost to time. In this subversion of mourning, the sightings of broken image files within the graveyard go from a minor nuisance to a moment of respect and grief of the cycle of digital life. Like us, the image files that build our internet have a limited lifespan— and whether it be because of malfunctioning code, decommissioned websites, or file hosting errors, they shall one day die too. In a world where any broken technology is considered fundamentally ‘useless’, ‘The Tomb of Wayward Images’ provides a space to slow down and reflect, as if it were a real graveyard.
Kennon Cummings

embeddings.title: Turnstime
embeddings.text:
Turnstime
Turnstime is an attempt to describe the reciprocal relationship of intuitive and infrastructural time by distilling a major logistic and economic engine of New York City: the public subway system. 

Two turnstiles rotate and tick at intervals relative to their respective station entries at the current time of day, visualizing and sonifying the people | workers | you and I flowing in from outer boroughs in the morning and back out in the evening. 
Proud Aiemruksa

embeddings.title: Prologue
embeddings.text:
Prologue
"Prologue" is an immersive VR experience where players become a baby soul, following their enchanting and emotional journey toward birth. In this dreamlike world above the clouds, players start in the luminous Castles of Light—a realm where unborn souls laugh, play, and seek for their future families, then they will be send down a slide to meet their family.
Jiayi Li

embeddings.title: MorphPlay
embeddings.text:
MorphPlay
How do we stay connected through play, memory, and sensory interaction? MorphPlay explores the bonds between people, reimagining attachment through the interplay of scent, memory, and shared experiences. At its heart is a plush bunny that "sniffs" you back, translating your scent into a whimsical memory-like description from a curated database.

Set within the framework of a toy chest designed for shared parent-child play, the project emphasizes the beauty of collaboration. The chest features two sets of building blocks: one simple and intuitive for a child, and another intricate and challenging for a parent. As users interact, MorphPlay layers sensory storytelling through the bunny, which responds to proximity by generating evocative scent-based memories. Each interaction triggers text-to-speech narration and a hazy projection, blending humor with the ephemeral nature of memory.

Inspired by Ani Liu’s Olfactory Time Capsule and the book Meaningful Differences, MorphPlay draws on the profound role of shared sensory and emotional experiences. It uses open-source tools like Arduino and MadMapper to create a playful yet thought-provoking exploration of presence and absence.

The piece also considers sustainability in its design. By investigating rechargeable sodium-ion battery systems as an alternative to disposable power sources, it aligns technological interactivity with environmental consciousness.

MorphPlay invites viewers to ask: How do sensory experiences—like scent—hold relationships together? Can a memory-like description or playful interaction replicate the warmth of presence? Through humor, curiosity, and sensory immersion, MorphPlay engages audiences in a tender exploration of connection, nostalgia, and the complexity of human attachment.
Anshula Saha

embeddings.title: Echo of The Canvas
embeddings.text:
Echo of The Canvas
Echo of the Canvas is an interactive artwork that explores animism by reimagining the relationship between viewers and art. Designed as an abstract painting with textured hills, the piece invites physical interaction through buttons atop each hill.

When a button is pressed, the “spirit” of the painting appears on a connected screen, performing a unique sequence of movements and sounds. These playful and dynamic responses create the illusion that the artwork is alive, engaging in a personal exchange with its audience.

The project challenges the passive nature of art observation, transforming the act of viewing into a two-way interaction. By evoking the feeling of communicating with a living entity, Echo of the Canvas encourages viewers to reflect on their connection to art and the unseen forces that animate the world around them.

Jingbo Ma

embeddings.title: Citriffany
embeddings.text:
Citriffany
In terms of appearance, this work is a self-designed-and-made Tiffany-style chandelier. It is inspired by citrus fruits, the colors of food, and Tiffany lamps. The artist sliced various citrus fruits, dried them at low temperatures, and carefully assembled them into a lampshade shape using transparent fishing lines. Through the citrus lampshade, one can observe the rich orange-yellow hues, dynamic light, and shadow effects and enjoy a refreshing citrus fragrance if one comes close.

Each fruit and every dried citrus slice is one of a kind. Like Tiffany glass, this piece is entirely handmade, with each component being irreplaceable and impossible to replicate. Speaking of differences, Tiffany glass is renowned for its elegant and intricate patterns. While citrus slices cannot form specific designs, the visible texture of the fruit, unlike the smoothness of glass, is a unique feature of this work. Inspired by an accidental mistake during the experimental phase, the artist challenged stereotypes of citrus slices by using longitudinal cuts, revealing unusual textures, and creating unique light and shadow effects.

Gently make it spin. And enjoy.
Amelia Shao

embeddings.title: Dancing Instruments
embeddings.text:
Dancing Instruments
Make music through dance. Gather three of your friends and place different shapes on the screen. As you dance and hit your assigned shapes, those shapes will start making music. 
Andi Jegeni

embeddings.title: Lantern of Connection
embeddings.text:
Lantern of Connection
A Wish Lantern is an interactive installation inspired by the Korean lantern festival (연등(燃燈)) and the tradition of making wishes for happiness, wellness, and good fortune. Drawing on the cultural symbolism of lanterns as sources of guidance and hope, it reimagines a time-honored custom within a contemporary setting, encouraging direct participation and personal connection.

Visitors are invited to insert a special coin inside the lantern. Each coin intensifies the lantern’s glow, weaving personal hopes into a collective tapestry of light. In return, the lantern releases a “lucky coin”—a symbolic token of a wish fulfilled—offering a tangible reminder of that shared moment.

Through this simple exchange, A Wish Lantern reflects the enduring human desire to find light in the darkness and to unite individual aspirations with a communal spirit. It encourages reflection on cultural continuity, the evolution of traditions, and how small gestures can foster deeper understanding. Ultimately, it celebrates the power of collective hope, demonstrating that what shines brightest often emerges from many hands, each contributing its own wish for the future.
Luna Park

embeddings.title: Paper House
embeddings.text:
Paper House
Paper House is a 3D animation exploring the paradox of inner sanctuary as both refuge and restraint. It reflects on the tension between the protection offered by internal voices and the limitations they impose, questioning how the structures we build for safety also shape and confine us, balancing connection with the outside world and self-imposed boundaries.

Emily Hu

embeddings.title: Sid the Squid
embeddings.text:
Sid the Squid
A wearable squid plush that clips onto hair. The squid lights up with different colors depending on which way you tilt it. Each gesture and color have their own connection.
Carol Yufei Wu

embeddings.title: Touch Grass
embeddings.text:
Touch Grass
Touch Grass is a collective experience about connection to the fabric of democracy, making a play on the cultural meme & phrase "Touch Grass". As you touch grass, images related to real time news headlines start to dissipate and the projection turns into a pond with flowers and peaceful music. If you let go, the spot you were holding on to becomes noisy again with real time news titles. Coming together and getting past the noise is the only way we can make change. Concept touches on the fact that it needs multiple people to get past the noise.
Inês Lucas

embeddings.title: Moodbox: The moodpicking jukebox
embeddings.text:
Moodbox: The moodpicking jukebox
Moodbox is a cute little shape jukebox that lets you set the mood for your day. It’ll give you a quote, whether it’s warm, silly, or even a little roast, depending on what you choose. It’s meant to be taken lightly and used to brighten up your day.
Billy Fadhila

embeddings.title: GJ Controller
embeddings.text:
GJ Controller
The GJ Controller is a custom-built electronic instrument that bridges the gap between traditional DJing and the electric guitar. This handcrafted device features an intuitive interface for precise control of DJ essentials while expanding performance and expressive possibilities. Communicating via MIDI, it is compatible with DJ software like Traktor, Serato, and Ableton Live and is fully customizable to suit any DJ or performance style.

Constructed over 7 weeks, the GJ Controller uses an Arduino Mega microcontroller, 5 protoboards, 18 buttons with LED control, a Guitar Hero-style “strum bar,” 8 potentiometers, a Pioneer crossfader, and over 100 wires. It allows control of DJ software or a DAW through its "Neck" and "Body."

The Neck features 9 buttons with LED feedback: 4 control cue points, 4 manage track stems (vocals, instruments, bass, drums), and 1 A/B Deck switch to alternate controls between Decks A and B. Each button requires activation with the “strum bar,” creating a visual performance element for the audience.

The Body operates independently of the strum bar, offering control over EQ, pitch, track selection, and blending via the crossfader.

The GJ Controller was conceptualized and performed by artist and creator “Tofu Jack,” who drew inspiration from his experience playing electric guitar and DJing. His curiosity about merging the performance aspects of both disciplines led to the creation of this innovative instrument.
Ian Pelton

embeddings.title: Doom & Bloom Game
embeddings.text:
Doom & Bloom Game
Doom & Bloom is a hilariously collaborative board game with an innovative open world layout which "blooms" from a shelter into a playable surface. Set in an apocalyptic future, players must gain life points by surviving every-worsening disasters by gathering resources, collecting absurd items, and helping save each other from illness. The game blends comedy, futurism, and aesthetic design to bring people closer even as the end of the world approaches. 
angela juarez

embeddings.title: In Between
embeddings.text:
In Between
In Between captures the experience of being stuck between childhood and adulthood. The body grows into adulthood, but the mind lingers in a younger, undefined state, holding onto the freedom and comfort of childhood. This gray area, neither fully child nor fully adult, carries both nostalgia for the past and the pressure to keep moving forward with time.
Lucia Shui

embeddings.title: Pebble
embeddings.text:
Pebble
Pebble is a revolutionary wearable ecosystem designed to bridge traditional in-person social interactions with cutting-edge AI assistance. It caters specifically to individuals who are neurodiverse, introverted, or socially anxious, enabling them to build meaningful personal and professional connections.
