By blending advanced technology with organic, real-time interactions, Pebble empowers users to expand their social skills, meet like-minded individuals, and foster genuine in-person relationships.

The Pebble ecosystem consists of three core components:
Fashionable Wearable Devices: Including a stylish necklace and a watch, these devices double as digital tools while seamlessly blending into everyday attire.
Mobile Application: A centralized hub that provides a summary of daily interactions, access to details about the people you’ve met, and an overview of shared conversations.

The wearable devices discreetly assist users in real time by identifying common interests, goals, and hobbies with others nearby. They encourage in-person connections with confidence, while maintaining the authenticity of face-to-face communication helping users develop essential social skills simultaneously.

Pebble bridges the gap between the physical and digital worlds. It helps users connect with vetted, like-minded individuals, fostering genuine interactions which helps to grow one’s social circle organically, improving both personal and professional relationships in a meaningful and lasting way.
Rajeshwari Ranjeet Kotwal

embeddings.title: Dislike & Disagree
embeddings.text:
Dislike & Disagree
Humans are usually more motivated towards disagreements and grouping ourselves based on common beliefs. Social media platforms, driven by profit, often exploit these tendencies by promoting divisive content. This leads to echo chambers and hinders productive discourse.

To counter this, I propose positively leveraging these natural human drives. By creating connections based on seemingly arbitrary dislikes, we can foster a sense of community among people with diverse viewpoints. This shared connection can then serve as a foundation for more constructive dialogue.

The goal is to design a space that encourages respectful debate and the exploration of different perspectives. By fostering empathy and understanding, we can bridge divides and find common ground, ultimately leading to more informed and productive discussions.
Caroline Sekar

embeddings.title: Cave of Fractal
embeddings.text:
Cave of Fractal
<Cave of Fractal> is inspired by the Allegory of the Cave. In this allegory, people gaze at the shadows of themselves on the cave wall day after day, trying to interpret the small movements of the shadows, but they fail to understand their own existence and the much larger world outside the cave. When people focus on their own lives, they often find it hard to imagine how vast or how small they can be at the same time. We focus on the dimension of our own lives, casting aside other larger or smaller dimensions.
In <Cave of Fractal>, the audience will explore within a continuous fractal structure, searching for another version of themselves, experiencing the dual nature of their existence—both 'on the outside' and 'in the inner' at the same time.

Jiyou Park

embeddings.title: Room - Remix
embeddings.text:
Room - Remix
Room - Remix is an interactive project that delves into the interplay between image and sound, as well as the dynamics of physical and digital spaces. Presented as an immersive 3D environment developed in Unity, it reimagines and remixes a personal space. Audiences engage with the textures and elements of this virtual space through a Playtron controller, allowing them to remix the room's sounds and textures.

Hazel He

embeddings.title: Amalgamation
embeddings.text:
Amalgamation
Amalgamation is an immersive installation that explores the fluidity of identity and the tension between societal expectations and personal authenticity. Featuring two synchronized projections—a floor projection evoking the depth and fluidity of water, and a vertical projection on sheer fabric—the work creates a meditative environment. These visuals, developed using TouchDesigner, AI interpolation, photography, and film editing, are accompanied by an atmospheric audio landscape with multilingual voiceovers and ambient sounds.

The installation uses water as a central metaphor, symbolizing transformation, reflection, and the liminal space between public and private selves. It critiques societal pressures to conform to idealized categories while celebrating the contradictions and fluidity that define individuality. Drawing on Western and Eastern cultural philosophies, Amalgamation contrasts the drive for control and categorization with the acceptance of life’s natural flow, inviting visitors to reflect on their evolving sense of self.

Inspired by mythological and historical water imagery—from Narcissus’s self-obsession to the communal and sanctuary-like roles of lakes and ponds—the installation blurs boundaries between self and other, real and imagined. Through its nonlinear narrative and hypnotic interplay of visuals and sound, Amalgamation offers a space for introspection, encouraging visitors to pause, embrace ambiguity, and reconsider their identity as an ever-changing amalgamation of experiences and influences.
Christie Kim

embeddings.title: Beneath the Waves
embeddings.text:
Beneath the Waves
Step inside an immersive box that recreates an underwater experience, where your breath and head movement work together to interact with a simulated aquatic environment. Your inhaling and exhaling into a mouthpiece control the movement of the group fish on the screen, and your head movement, tracked by head tracking, determines where the bubbles appear in the underwater world. The experience reflects the subtle impact of human presence on the ocean and its creatures.
Laurel Fang

embeddings.title: Kinetic Origami
embeddings.text:
Kinetic Origami 
Interactive Origami Piece
This project is an interactive kinetic sculpture inspired by the art of origami. It features 16 linear actuators that dynamically open and close the origami shape, mimicking the movement of an umbrella. The piece responds to the viewer’s motion, creating a mesmerizing interaction between art and technology. This sculpture explores the harmony between human presence and mechanical design. 
Parth Pawar

embeddings.title: The Ten Years Journey of a Balloon
embeddings.text:
The Ten Years Journey of a Balloon
This project invites users to step into the life of a red balloon that embarks on a ten-year journey through New York City after slipping from a child’s hands in Times Square in 2014. It combines interactive storytelling, educational elements, and immersive technology to explore NYC’s transformation over the past decade. Users take control of the balloon through a series of interactive scenes: playing a flappy bird game on top of Central Park to witness its seasons, navigating urban developments like Citibike and MoMA through interactive collages, and battling gusts of wind as the balloon descends to reunite with its owner—now an adult. The experience blends emotional narrative with playful challenges, utilizing technologies like mouse, keyboard, or hand posture  interactions. Educational moments highlight NYC’s cultural and technological progress, making this project both entertaining and thought-provoking.
Lisa Liu

embeddings.title: The Morph
embeddings.text:
The Morph
This immersive performance explores themes of identity, transformation, and the conflict between one’s authentic self and the weight of external influences.

It features a single performer whose movements are captured in real-time using motion capture (mocap) technology, transmitting the data into Unreal Engine 5 to animate a digital humanoid creature. The creature evolves visually and conceptually as it interacts with the digital environment.
Damon Chen

embeddings.title: Slipper Flipper
embeddings.text:
Slipper Flipper 
Have you ever been to a hotel went to bed and when you get up the next morning the slippers are facing the wrong way? That's no longer going to be a problem with the Slipper Flipper! 

The Slipper Flipper automatically flips whenever you take them off so they're ALWAYS facing the correct side!
Angel Wong

embeddings.title: Play
embeddings.text:
Play 
A sensory experience where you confront yourself.
MJ Zhou

embeddings.title: Virtual Turtle Walk
embeddings.text:
Virtual Turtle Walk
Virtual Turtle Walk is an interactive project inspired by real-life "turtle walks," where volunteers help protect baby sea turtles. Globally, conservationists walk along shores to collect turtle eggs and safeguard them from predators and environmental threat. When the eggs hatch, volunteers use flashlights to guide the baby turtles to the ocean. Without this intervention, hatchlings often move inland, drawn by city lights instead of the moonlit horizon.
In our project, this experience is recreated in a virtual world using Ultraleap’s hand-tracking. Users insert their hand through a box and their hand movements create a beam of light on the virtual beach sand. The baby turtles in the scene start walking in the wrong direction and the user needs to guide them to the ocean using the light. The turtles follow wherever the user moves their hand, creating a realistic and engaging experience.
This project is designed to teach people about the challenges turtles face and the importance of conservation. By letting users take part in guiding the turtles, it helps them understand the role humans can play in protecting wildlife. The intuitive hand-tracking makes the interaction accessible and enjoyable for all ages while addressing critical issues like light pollution and habitat protection. Virtual Turtle Walk combines technology and storytelling to inspire empathy and action for sea turtle conservation, making it a meaningful and educational experience.
Shri Ranjani Ramakrishnan

embeddings.title: Common Sense
embeddings.text:
Common Sense
Common Sense is a generative comic which explores the interpretative and representational capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs). By fine-tuning a vision model on 100 original graphics and connecting it with an LLM tailored to our liking, we explore notions of authorship and collaboration between humans and today's intelligent, artificial co-pilots.

Wallis Millar-Blanchaer

embeddings.title: Paper Automatons
embeddings.text:
Paper Automatons
This is a set of automatons made of paper -- designed, printed, cut, folded, glued… And they can move. For the Winter Show 2024, I'm showcasing particularly one complicated paper automaton, The Rolling Reels Circus, designed by PaperPino and crafted by me and Isabel, and a few “machines” from our ITP woodshop designed and crafted by me. A few templates of the machines are available on the table – feel free to grab one and have fun making a tiny paper automaton of your own!
Isabel Wu

embeddings.title: Particle
embeddings.text:
Particle
Particle is an on-demand, ambient interface for public and personal health. More specifically, it’s an air-quality monitoring system that relies on social contributions mapped to hard data to generate awareness and an understanding of the health of the environments we spend time within. 

As a pilot, the system has been installed in the NYU fabrication shop space to provide real-world insights to the ITP/IMA community. The project consists of sensor hardware, a projection-based ambient interface and a web experience that allows for a data deep dive and user contributions. 

The project compels us to question our built environments and the materials and practices we employ in our everyday lives as they relate to our long-term health and well-being. Particle’s interface – spanning between projection and our devices – provides stakeholders with an experience that is on-demand and informative as needed. 

Steven Jos Phan

embeddings.title: Suture
embeddings.text:
Suture
Suture is a wearable project exploring the relationship between humans and plants. In today's world, where countless pressures weigh heavily on us, people's mental well-being has been deeply fragmented. In response, I began seeking strength from plants. With their remarkable self-healing abilities, they embody resilience— even when broken in half, they quietly mend their wounds and emerge renewed. Just as plants transform pain into growth, this project aims to explore the power of resilience and self-recovery, drawing inspiration from nature's ability to heal and thrive amidst adversity.
Zijin Huang

embeddings.title: Afterlife
embeddings.text:
Afterlife
Afterlife is a poetic exploration of a hybrid world, a lost civilization where machines and nature have merged to form an ecology on a deserted planet years after humans have disappeared. The boundaries between the artificial and the organic blur, telling the story of evolution beyond humanity.
Yifan Chen

embeddings.title: Spooky Music Box
embeddings.text:
Spooky Music Box
A musical instrument combined with a stage lighting experience. When each character blocks light on the optical sensor, sound and light are activated. Once all five different sounds are harmonized, additional stage lights appear. The tempo and pitch can be controlled, similar to the DJ-ing experience.
Jakyoung Goo

embeddings.title: Sixty Worlds - Demo
embeddings.text:
Sixty Worlds - Demo
The Sixty Worlds is a website (sixtyworlds.com) where users can share their 3D models of virtual worlds, as a place to showcase their work, get feedback and contribute to the community of virtual space design. It will be the only website that you can actually visit and tour inside of the models like a visitor. 
As a former architect and a present game designer, I understand how things are at the beginning of creating a virtual world. People strive for references, scales, adaptation to real worlds, reading plans, elevations and sections, building human scales… but nothing compares to learning from an existing project. 
In addition to giving space designers a kickstart, this website is also going to collect feedback and quantitative data. It would possibly be the first time in history to evaluate spaces with data in equal conditions.

Jiaqi Yi

embeddings.title: "Chance Me"
embeddings.text:
"Chance Me"
"Chance Me" is about self-judgment and external validation in the process of college applications. Fragments of identity—scores, extracurriculars, essays—are displayed, distorted, and reduced to a single number. Yet, the question remains: how much of this system reflects you, and how much do you reflect the system?

I construct and deconstruct audiences captured by the webcam to fit an imagined algorithm, to be reduced to something measurable, digestible, and ultimately disposable.
Muyuan Li

embeddings.title: Cyber Blossom
embeddings.text:
Cyber Blossom
Cyber Bloom merges the organic and the digital, inviting participants into an interactive ecosystem where digital plants thrive in response to human actions. By blending speculative technology with the natural world, this project explores the future of human interaction with digital ecosystems, where the boundaries between the organic and the artificial blur.
When audience arrive, they are greeted by digital flowers blooming on a screen. Through actions like watering, adjusting light, and exhaling CO2, users interact with the real-world soil, influencing the growth and blossom of the digital plants in real time. 
This project challenges traditional ideas of nature and care, proposing a world where human actions shape not only the physical environment but also digital and virtual spaces. Cyber Bloom is both playful and thought-provoking, inviting reflection on how the rise of cyborg-like interactions—where humans and technology coalesce—could redefine our relationship with the natural world. In this speculative future, the line between nature, technology, and identity becomes ever more fluid, offering a new perspective on how we coexist with the environments we create.
Ivy Jiang

embeddings.title: ALOE LOVE FOR YOU
embeddings.text:
ALOE LOVE FOR YOU
ALOE LOVE FOR YOU is a site-specific art piece for Al Oerter Recreation Center in Flushing, Queens. Al Oerter is one of the busiest NYC Parks recreation centers in the borough and hundreds of people frequent the center each day to work out, make friends, and enrich their lives physically and mentally.

There is a micro:bit to promote S.T.E.A.M. programming at the center as well as audio by incredible 2024 center managers, Ms Angela Elie and Ms Tammy Mitchel. I have worked at this center with them and so many wonderful colleagues. The staff makes this space a welcoming and safe environment that people genuinely look forward to being in. The staff truly makes this center special, so I created this gift to appreciate them (past, current, and staff who may work here in the future too). 

A QR code to the center's weekly schedule is engraved for members of the public to use. They can also interact with the joyous arcade buttons.

A lot of love for my Al-Oerter community, always!
Sidikha Ashraf

embeddings.title: My Room
embeddings.text:
My Room
My Room is a first-person narrative digital experience that details my memories and experiences throughout my time at New York University. I made this project to explore how we tie memories to physical spaces and challenge how we perceive and share our personal lives in an increasingly superficial world. The outcome of my work is an incredibly personal digital journey that details my growth throughout college. Players can step into my shoes and experience, first-hand, the key moments that shaped my college career. In today’s world, we get to pick and choose what aspects of our lives to share with others. With this project, I want to highlight the highs and lows of being a college student in New York. By immersing players in my memories, the joy, the struggles, and the in-between moments, I hope to inspire them to reflect on their own lives and find solace in the shared complexity of human experience.
Drew Brown

embeddings.title: Elemental Island
embeddings.text:
Elemental Island
In today's fast world, people hardly get the chance to reconnect with themselves and nature. The Elemental Island is a portable meditation toolkit inspired by Duchamp's suitcase art and the ancient philosophy of the Three Elements-wood, fire, and water-rooted in East Asian culture. This compact suitcase houses three compartments, each representing one of the elements. Participants engage with these elements through tactile components, sensors, soothing sounds, and visuals. For example, the interaction with the wood element evokes the calm of a forest, fire inspires warmth and energy, and water brings the serene flow of a stream. When these components are put into slots, they trigger certain virtual environments on a screen. Such interaction seamlessly bridges the physical and digital experiences to foster moments of mindfulness and reflection in the chaos of the city. The Elemental Island blends ancient wisdom with modern design to create a personal oasis for meditation and balance. Whether at home, in the office, or outdoors, it serves as a reminder to pause, reconnect, and rediscover harmony with oneself and nature.
Rachel Shin

embeddings.title: Web The Hack
embeddings.text:
Web The Hack
A program that can put the participant into about 40% of the world's website. Using Tensorflow, the program allows the participant to knock off content on the website by moving their hands.
Zongze Chen

embeddings.title: MindFlutter
embeddings.text:
MindFlutter
MindFlutter is an interactive projection installation that bridges the human mind and technology through brainwave-controlled servos and TouchDesigner. This innovative artwork translates focus levels into tangible, dynamic visuals and movements, merging physical and digital realms to create a multi-sensory experience.

At its core, the installation uses brainwave data to manipulate 3D-printed flowers attached to servos. As participants focus, their brainwave intensity is divided into four distinct levels:

Focus Level 1 (10–20): Servo 1 rotates, animating its flower.
Focus Level 2 (20–30): Servo 2 activates, bringing its flower to life.
Focus Level 3 (30–40): Servo 3 moves, extending the floral choreography.
Focus Level 4 (>40): Servo 4 rotates, and a large, radiant butterfly is projected across the screen, symbolizing peak focus and mental clarity.
This delicate interplay of mechanics, projection, and neurotechnology creates a poetic dialogue between the mind and the environment. As participants interact with the installation, they witness their focus materialize, fostering mindfulness and engagement in an immersive setting.
Taigen Jin

embeddings.title: Tracing Fractures
embeddings.text:
Tracing Fractures
Tracing Fractures is an interactive installation featuring a ceramic bowl repaired with gold, inspired by the Japanese art of kintsugi. Participants are invited to run their hands along the bowl's touch-sensitive surface, exploring its intricate cartography of golden seams. As hands move across the repaired fractures, the installation responds with a choreographed interplay of light and sound, creating a therapeutic sensory experience. This piece aims to transform the concept of damage and repair into a self-reflective journey, encouraging viewers to contemplate the imperfect process of healing. 
Audrey Oh

embeddings.title: Sound Bubbles
embeddings.text:
Sound Bubbles
Sound Bubbles is a design and research piece that explores how we interact with spatial audio through a fun and tactile interface. Moving beyond traditional single-knob controllers and complex DAW interfaces, this work invites exploration into a spatialized sound environment through elegant simplicity.

Sound Bubbles consists of four precision knobs and a multifunctional button. Three knobs map directly to spatial coordinates (X, Y, Z), allowing listeners to position sound sources anywhere in three-dimensional space. The fourth knob controls volume, and the button manages sound sources – adding, removing, or selecting between them.

Rather than prescribe how to interact with spatialized sound, Sound Bubbles encourages natural discovery. It is designed in a minimalist way to foster curiosity, inviting users to explore and understand spatial relationships through direct manipulation and active listening.
Yifan Deng

embeddings.title: Dear Vincent...
embeddings.text:
Dear Vincent...
What constitutes of an digital image? Every amazing painting or imagery we see on screen granted is but a combination of dots and lines… Use the morse code keyer - the oldest method of digital & serial communication - to unmask the paintings of Vincent Van Gogh, the artist who's creations would have gone untold without his communication to his brother Theo through telegraphs.
Cheewon Choi

embeddings.title: Wings of Expression
embeddings.text:
Wings of Expression
Combining the aesthetics of Gundam parts and technology, resulting in a mobile attachment for headphones that moves in response to hand gestures. The attachment brings a futuristic and personalized element to everyday items, allowing users to communicate non-verbally using mechanical movements.
Julie Chen

embeddings.title: Pixy
embeddings.text:
Pixy
Pixy is a furry, robotic pet. It is a robot stuffed inside a plush toy that interacts with the users, just like a real pet. When you pet and scratch it, or when you hold it up and rock it, Pixy shakes its head and purrs. You can also talk to them, and they will respond to you, of course, in their own language.

What sets it apart from the traditional stuffed animals is its interactivity—it’s every child’s dream to own a toy that moves and talks to them. The motions and movements, though simple at the current stage, bring life to an item designed to resemble real life that would otherwise be static. The level of companion and emotional support, the feeling of “connectedness”, is now enhanced.

It’s more distinguished purpose, a robotic pet, serves as an alternative to traditional pet keeping that come at rather high stakes. Pixy is a pet that you will never have to clean after nor feel compelled to walk on a daily basis. You won’t get allergies from it, and bills from the vet or Petco will likewise never be an issue. The palm-sized buddy can also fit inside your pocket and pass any securities checks, keeping you accompanied at all times. And, above all, its life is never at risk, making it a true companion for a lifetime. Low cost, low stakes, low responsibilities, and no allergies whatsoever. Now nothing stands between you and your long-wanted furry friend.

Lihan Bao

embeddings.title: Courage Unboxed
embeddings.text:
Courage Unboxed
Everyone harbors fears deep within, often hidden or avoided. Courage Unboxed is an interactive game experience created with p5.js, designed to guide participants in confronting these fears and taking courageous steps forward through exploration and persistence. In this immersive journey, players navigate a dark space, uncovering blocks that symbolize courage. Black blocks add points to the player’s score, representing each bold step forward, while red blocks signify the small challenges or setbacks encountered along the way.
The game progresses through five levels, each becoming easier to reflect how fear diminishes through continuous confrontation. In the final scene, players are met with one of two outcomes, Overcoming Fear: Chaotic scribbles transform into a glowing yellow circle, symbolizing growth and triumph, accompanied by an uplifting message such as “You made a big step.” Or Making Progress: Progress is celebrated with a message like “You made some progress,” encouraging further efforts.
At the end of the experience, players are invited to draw a keepsake from a box, such as a keychain engraved with a random positive quote. This serves as a tangible reminder of their bravery. Those who achieve a perfect score or fulfill special conditions unlock a unique keepsake, rewarding their exceptional journey.Courage Unboxed celebrates the act of facing fear head-on, no matter how small or large the steps may be. It’s a reminder that every effort counts, and the courage to confront what lies within is the first step toward growth and self-discovery.
Silvia Zhou

embeddings.title: Shopping Maniac
embeddings.text:
Shopping Maniac
"Shopping Maniac" transforms a real shopping cart into a game controller, combining physical movement with digital gameplay to deliver a playful shopping experience. Players race against the clock to collect as many items as possible and achieve a high score.
Duban Morales

embeddings.title: DoNotDisturb/DoAbsurd
embeddings.text:
DoNotDisturb/DoAbsurd
This is a Do Not Disturb Sign for an Absurd Hotel. When you are traveling, what's the one thing that you often have to wash by hand? For us, it's the sock. Our Do Not Disturb Sign doubles up as a sock drying apparatus, speed up the drying process by spinning it. The drying process starts when you lock the hotel door, and blocks the entry/exit as long as the sock is not dry yet. 
Una Zhang

embeddings.title: Composition for Understanding Identities
embeddings.text:
Composition for Understanding Identities

embeddings.title: Hands of Creation
embeddings.text:
Hands of Creation 
This interactive digital art project explores the dynamic relationships between space, matter, and human agency through a particle system controlled by hand gestures. Particles, as the fundamental units of matter, form the visual and conceptual basis of the work, transitioning from chaotic dispersion to precise geometric structures. This transformation reflects the tension between randomness and order, serving as a metaphor for the human impulse to impose structure and meaning onto complexity.

The project invites users to manipulate thousands of particles with hand gestures, highlighting their innate capacity to create and control. It portrays creation as a dynamic interplay between intention and emergence, where users guide but do not fully dictate the system’s outcomes. Geometric forms, central to the work’s conceptual framework, emerge from initial chaos to symbolize the human drive to organize and understand the world.

By using hand gestures as the interface, the project emphasizes the intimate connection between physical movement and digital interaction. Hands—our earliest tools for creation—become a means of shaping emergent digital environments, transforming abstract particles into structured forms. This tactile interaction underscores the user’s agency while exploring the boundaries between control and randomness, and between human intention and computational possibilities.

Through distinct geometric transformations, the piece challenges perceptions of materiality, showing objects as fluid, dynamic systems rather than static entities. It becomes a meditation on how we interact with technology, revealing a creative dialogue between human expression and computational processes. The experience reflects on our inherent desire to make sense of complexity, presenting the act of creation as a powerful synthesis of human ingenuity and emergent systems.
Ege Tezcan

embeddings.title: Study Ball: A Revolutionary Interactive Learning Tool
embeddings.text:
Study Ball: A Revolutionary Interactive Learning Tool
The Study Ball is a groundbreaking device designed to transform the way you learn, offering a tactile and interactive study experience that makes learning fun and effective. Unlike traditional study methods, Study Ball combines the thrill of trivia with the power of repetition, creating an engaging way to reinforce key concepts and boost retention.

At its core, Study Ball is equipped with hundreds of questions across various subjects, ranging from art and science to vocabulary and math. This diverse range of topics ensures that learners of all ages and academic levels can benefit from its use. The device is designed to make learning an active, hands-on process. Simply select a subject, and Study Ball will prompt you with a series of questions to test your knowledge.

What sets Study Ball apart is its focus on repetition. By engaging with the device repeatedly, you strengthen your memory and comprehension, which leads to deeper understanding and longer-lasting retention. The device's simple interface allows users to focus on learning without distractions, while its engaging format makes studying less intimidating and more enjoyable.

Whether you're preparing for exams, mastering new skills, or just looking to expand your knowledge, Study Ball turns studying into an interactive, rewarding experience. Perfect for solo study sessions or group learning, it supports a personalized approach to education and enhances overall learning effectiveness.
Samuel Oge

embeddings.title: Art Board
embeddings.text:
Art Board
Multisensory Artboard, is an interactive installation designed to empower individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD), including Autism Spectrum Disorders, by providing an accessible and creative outlet for self-expression. Inspired by the calming and dynamic elements of nature, the artboard transforms touch and sensory interactions into vivid digital artworks. Users engage with textured surfaces and sensors connected to p5.js, generating personalized visuals displayed on a screen. The designs evoke themes such as counting stars, shifting seasons, and changing landscapes, offering a serene yet engaging experience. To ensure inclusivity, the installation incorporates ADA-compliant features for wheelchair users. Every creation is uniquely personal, with an option to print the artwork as a keepsake. In a separate immersive room, projection mapping enhances the sensory experience by combining visuals, sounds, and scents, bringing the outdoors indoors. By blending art, technology, and multisensory engagement, this project fosters creativity and connection, inviting audiences to explore the boundless possibilities of nature-inspired expression.
Aradhita Maheshwari

embeddings.title: Bento
embeddings.text:
Bento 
The Absurd Bento Box Experience playfully reimagines Japanese bento culture, blending the eccentric creativity of *Kenji Kawakami*, the inventor of Chindōgu, with the refined minimalism of *Muji CEO Kenya Hara*.  

This oversized, interactive bento box transforms dining into an immersive ritual. Designed with four drawers, each represents a course in a traditional four-course meal. The journey begins when a user drops a fish into the box’s central hole. Upon detection, the mechanism triggers one drawer to open, revealing the next course and rewarding the participant with a moment of surprise and delight.  

Celebrating Japan’s tradition of craftsmanship, this absurd yet elegant creation questions the boundaries of utility and play. It invites users to experience the dining process as a collaborative and interactive art form, rather than a passive act.  

The Absurd Bento Box Experience is more than a meal—it’s a multisensory exploration of joy, curiosity, and cultural storytelling.
Arya Bansal

The Misfortune Cookie
Misfortune Cookies is an interactive experience exposing the realities of hate crimes through a familiar cultural symbol. Users shatter a giant virtual fortune cookie with their hand movements, unveiling shocking headlines of violence and discrimination hidden inside. This project utilizes a Kinect camera, Unreal Engine 5, and TouchDesigner to merge interactivity and powerful storytelling, confronting viewers with the weight of unspoken truths while challenging the societal tendency to ignore these injustices.
Josh Sun

Grip-X
Grip-X is a robotic claw controlled by finger gestures, combining machine learning, Arduino, p5.js, physical computing, and engineering. Using ml5.js for finger gesture recognition, it detects finger movement through the website live camera and translates it into precise control of the arm and claw with 3 servo motors. My inspiration for this work was designed as a mobility aid for individuals with muscle weakness, who are unable to perform strong movements, or a rehabilitation tool offering innovative assistance.

embeddings.text:
。Period 。
The menstrual period has been a subject of taboo for centuries across different cultures, and unnecessarily encouraged to be avoided, concealed, and sometimes misunderstood associated with exaggeration.
While society progressed, as of currently in 2024, there still lacks sufficient understanding, acknowledgment, and empathy of menstruation—be it its form, the cost, and accommodation, or multiple aspects that may influence a person—and even among people who are in their menstruating years, each individual’s experiences differ, and often the intensity of how much a person is affected needs to be justified. 
The artist found solace when other people acknowledge in surprise—at the sight of the amount of blood and with the sound of the uterus’s tiny explosion—that it is indeed some intense and heavy period, and would hope that people who suffer/simply go through menstruation would not need any justification to consolidate their recurring biological and mental experience. 
Chienn Tai

embeddings.title: ctrl + alt + light
embeddings.text:
ctrl + alt + light
Can adding seemingly trivial details to mundane things transform how we perceive them and value the world? Ctrl + alt + light is a nontraditional lamp that aims to challenge our ideas about scale and our relationship to ordinary objects. It presents light in a whimsical way by using the shape of oversized keycaps from a keyboard while retaining the functionality of a lamp, suitable for everyday use. Users can interact with it by pressing the keys to control the power and appearance of the light. The fabrication aligns with the range of custom designs created in the growing community of mechanical keyboard enthusiasts. The lamp’s pixel style and color palette also specifically draw inspiration from the earlier nostalgic days of mechanical keyboards and the Y2K aesthetic.
Myrah Sarwar
